body.name: current-state recursive agenda compiler
body.construction:
For a nonterminal encoded state \(\zeta\), let the current task be the lexicographically least unfinished labelled kernel block under \(\operatorname{enc}_H\), and let \(G_\zeta\), \(R_\zeta\), and \(Y_\zeta\) denote its current CADMG, random mask, and local outcome mask. The deterministic compiler \(\operatorname{Comp}_H\) refreshes the agenda from the current state, rather than from a proposed derivation, as follows.

First form \(\mathsf G(\zeta)\), the lexicographically ordered list of all occurrences of stored selector multiplexers that are actually present in a current context-labelled kernel with context in \(H\). If \(\mathsf G(\zeta)\neq\varnothing\), set \(\Sigma=\mathsf G(\zeta)\) and set the other newly generated agenda lists to empty. Once \(\mathsf G(\zeta)=\varnothing\), assign each unfinished recursive district task the lexicographically least context in \(H\) satisfying its displayed laid-back or override values, graphical separation test, and reachability test, if such a context exists; otherwise retain its target-only-hole label. These are finite tests on the current stored graphs and kernels, and a failing context test creates no token. Select the least unfinished task, and define its fixing set to be empty when it has only a hole label. Apply the following mutually exclusive case list in the displayed order:
\[
 Z_\zeta=R_\zeta\setminus\operatorname{an}_{G_\zeta}(Y_\zeta),
 \qquad
 \mathsf D(\zeta)=\operatorname{dis}(G_\zeta),
 \qquad
 \mathsf W(\zeta)=
 \left\{W\in R_\zeta:
 \operatorname{dis}_{G_\zeta}(W)\cap
 \operatorname{de}_{G_\zeta}(W)=\{W\}
 \right\}.
\]
If \(Z_\zeta\neq\varnothing\), generate exactly the sum-elimination token for \(Z_\zeta\). Otherwise, if \(|\mathsf D(\zeta)|>1\), generate exactly the district-elimination token whose child tasks are the districts in encoded order, each queried on all of its vertices. Otherwise, if \(\mathsf W(\zeta)\neq\varnothing\), generate exactly the fixing token for the least element of \(\mathsf W(\zeta)\). Its margin certificate is computed, not postulated: put the finitely many current rational kernel cells over the common product of previously registered denominators, expand the finite sum over the alphabet of \(W\), recursively label every leaf by either a supported positive context cell or an earlier positive-ledger entry, cancel common factors, and verify the resulting polynomial identity by cross-multiplication. If all four predicates fail, declare the state residual-ready and generate the sole residual token. Its projection list starts with the canonical composite of the labelled sum, product, district, and fixing circuits already stored in the state and then lists the remaining circuits generated by the fixed labelled elimination order; its contrast list is the encoded signed-row-swap list. Thus residual-ready means
\[
 \mathsf G(\zeta)=\varnothing,
 \qquad Z_\zeta=\varnothing,
 \qquad |\mathsf D(\zeta)|=1,
 \qquad \mathsf W(\zeta)=\varnothing,
\]
independently of whether any residual candidate passes its verifier. All context, vertex, district, and circuit ties are broken by \(\operatorname{enc}_H\). After every admitted transition the compiler is rerun on the successor. No token that fails its current graphical predicate is placed on the refreshed agenda.
